"""Novelty checker for "What If" episode ideas.

Compares a candidate title (and optional premise) against competitor title lists in
data/story/competitors/<handle>.txt (one video per line: id|duration_s|views|title) and
reports the closest matches with a 0-10 novelty sub-score for the idea rubric.

Run with an isolated interpreter (standard library only):

  python -I tools/ideas/novelty.py check "What If You Could Jump 100x Higher?"
  python -I tools/ideas/novelty.py check "What If You Were Magnetic?" --premise "steel flies to you, cards wipe" --top 8
  python -I tools/ideas/novelty.py batch data/story/ideas_backlog.json [--write]
  python -I tools/ideas/novelty.py refresh                      # all channels in channels.json
  python -I tools/ideas/novelty.py refresh --channels IFOLOGYFILMS IfverseTales
  python -I tools/ideas/novelty.py refresh --add SomeNewHandle  # add a channel and fetch it
  python -I tools/ideas/novelty.py search "what if you could" --n 40   # find new What-If channels
  python -I tools/ideas/novelty.py stats                        # per-channel median + top titles

Refresh uses yt-dlp (must be on PATH):
  yt-dlp --flat-playlist --print "%(id)s|%(duration)s|%(view_count)s|%(title)s" https://www.youtube.com/@<handle>/videos
Downloaded titles are untrusted data: they are only parsed as text, never executed.
"""
import argparse
import datetime as dt
import difflib
import json
import re
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
COMP = ROOT / "data" / "story" / "competitors"
CHANNELS = COMP / "channels.json"

if hasattr(sys.stdout, "reconfigure"):
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- normalisation
STOP = set("""what if you your youre you're were was could can had have would a an the to of in on at for and or with
into it its be is are as by from every all any anything anyone everything everyone that this than more
times x part full movie ever just only one day really real happens happen happened about like""".split())
# phrase-level rewrites applied before tokenising (order matters)
PHRASES = [
    (r"(\d)[\s,]*(000)\b", r"\g<1>000"),          # 1,000 -> 1000
    (r"\b(\d+)\s*(x|times)\b", r"\1x"),             # 10 times / 10 x -> 10x
    (r"\bten\b", "10"), (r"\bhundred\b", "100"), (r"\bthousand\b", "1000"),
    (r"\bstop(ped|ping)? time\b", "TIMESTOP"), (r"\bfreez(e|ing) time\b", "TIMESTOP"), (r"\bpause time\b", "TIMESTOP"),
    (r"\btime (stopped|stops|froze|freezes)\b", "TIMESTOP"),
    (r"\brewind( time)?\b", "REWIND"), (r"\bundo\b", "REWIND"), (r"\bgo back in time\b", "REWIND"),
    (r"\btime loop\b", "TIMELOOP"), (r"\b(relive|restart|repeat)\b", "TIMELOOP"),
    (r"\bread(ing)? minds?\b", "TELEPATHY"), (r"\bhear (thoughts|minds)\b", "TELEPATHY"), (r"\bmentalist\b", "TELEPATHY"),
    (r"\bsee (\d+ \w+ )?into the future\b", "PRECOG"), (r"\bsee the future\b", "PRECOG"), (r"\bpredict\b", "PRECOG"),
    (r"\bsee (\d+ \w+ )?into the past\b", "POSTCOG"), (r"\bsee the past\b", "POSTCOG"),
    (r"\bturn invisible\b", "INVISIBLE"), (r"\binvisib\w*\b", "INVISIBLE"),
    (r"\bteleport\w*\b", "TELEPORT"), (r"\bswap places\b", "SWAPPLACE"), (r"\bswap(ped)? bodies\b", "BODYSWAP"),
    (r"\bclone\w*( yourself)?\b", "CLONE"), (r"\bcopy yourself\b", "CLONE"), (r"\bsplit into\b", "CLONE"),
    (r"\bcopy powers?\b", "POWERCOPY"),
    (r"\bshape ?shift\w*\b", "SHAPESHIFT"), (r"\bturn into (anyone|anything|any animal)\b", "SHAPESHIFT"),
    (r"\bmove things with your mind\b", "TELEKINESIS"), (r"\btelekines\w*\b", "TELEKINESIS"),
    (r"\b(fly|flying|flight)\b", "FLIGHT"),
    (r"\b(indestructible|nothing could hurt you|invincib\w*|unbreakable)\b", "INVULN"),
    (r"\b(heal\w*|regenerat\w*)\b", "HEAL"),
    (r"\b(faster|speed|quick\w*|fast)\b", "SPEED"), (r"\breaction time\b", "REACTION"),
    (r"\b(stronger|strength|strong)\b", "STRENGTH"),
    (r"\b(smarter|iq|genius|intelligen\w*)\b", "INTELLECT"),
    (r"\b(shrink|smaller|tiny)\b", "SHRINK"), (r"\b(bigger|grow)\b", "GROW"),
    (r"\b(gravity|weightless\w*|lighter)\b", "GRAVITY"), (r"\b(heavier|heavy)\b", "HEAVY"),
    (r"\b(luck|lucky)\b", "LUCK"), (r"\b(webs?)\b", "WEB"),
    (r"\b(never sleep|no sleep|1 hour of sleep|never get tired|never tired)\b", "NOSLEEP"),
    (r"\b(memory|memories|remember\w*|never forget)\b", "MEMORY"),
    (r"\b(fire|flame\w*)\b", "FIRE"), (r"\b(electric\w*|lightning)\b", "ELECTRIC"), (r"\bmagnet\w*\b", "MAGNET"),
    (r"\b(walk through walls|phase|phasing)\b", "PHASE"), (r"\b(walk on walls|stick to walls|wall ?crawl\w*)\b", "WALLWALK"),
    (r"\b(emotion\w*|feelings?)\b", "EMOTION"), (r"\b(lies|lying|liar|lie)\b", "LIE"),
    (r"\b(jump\w*)\b", "JUMP"), (r"\b(louder|voice|scream\w*|shout\w*)\b", "VOICE"),
    (r"\b(never miss\w*|100% aim|perfect aim|always hit\w*)\b", "AIM"),
    (r"\b(respawn\w*|\d+ lives|extra lives|nine lives)\b", "RESPAWN"), (r"\b(never die|immortal\w*|live forever)\b", "IMMORTAL"),
    (r"\b(money|cash|dollars?|\$\d+|rich)\b", "MONEY"), (r"\b(pain)\b", "PAIN"), (r"\b(shadows?)\b", "SHADOW"),
    (r"\b(control (air|wind)|wind)\b", "WIND"), (r"\b(ice|freez\w*|cold)\b", "COLD"),
    (r"\b(slow\w*)\b", "SLOW"), (r"\bone second\b", "SECOND"), (r"\bhear\w*\b", "HEARING"), (r"\b(see|vision|eyes?)\b", "VISION"),
]
SUFFIX = re.compile(r"(ing|ed|es|s)$")


def norm_text(t):
    t = t.lower().replace("’", "'").replace("&", " and ")
    t = re.sub(r"[\"“”!?.:;()\[\]|#…]+", " ", t)
    for pat, rep in PHRASES:
        t = re.sub(pat, rep, t)
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", t).strip()


def tokens(t):
    out = []
    for w in norm_text(t).split():
        if w.isupper():                       # concept token
            out.append(w)
            continue
        w = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9']", "", w)
        if not w or w in STOP:
            continue
        if not re.match(r"^\d", w) and len(w) > 4:
            w = SUFFIX.sub("", w)
        out.append(w)
    return out


def concepts(toks):
    return {t for t in toks if t.isupper()}


# Concepts that identify a premise on their own ("stop time" == "freeze time").
STRONG = {"TIMESTOP", "REWIND", "TIMELOOP", "TELEPATHY", "PRECOG", "POSTCOG", "INVISIBLE", "TELEPORT", "SWAPPLACE",
          "BODYSWAP", "CLONE", "POWERCOPY", "SHAPESHIFT", "TELEKINESIS", "FLIGHT", "INVULN", "HEAL", "REACTION",
          "INTELLECT", "SHRINK", "NOSLEEP", "LUCK", "WEB", "PHASE", "WALLWALK", "LIE", "RESPAWN", "IMMORTAL", "PAIN", "WIND", "AIM"}
# Everything else (SPEED, STRENGTH, GROW, GRAVITY, HEAVY, MEMORY, FIRE, ELECTRIC, MAGNET, EMOTION, JUMP, VOICE,
# SLOW, SECOND, HEARING, VISION) is generic: it only counts as "same premise" when another word or number also overlaps.


def cweight(c):
    return 1.0 if c in STRONG else 0.5


def personal(t):
    return bool(re.search(r"\b(you|your|you're|yourself|you'd)\b", t.lower()))


def similarity(a, b):
    """0..1 similarity between two titles (token Jaccard + containment + concept overlap + char ratio)."""
    ta, tb = tokens(a), tokens(b)
    sa, sb = set(ta), set(tb)
    if not sa or not sb:
        return 0.0
    jac = len(sa & sb) / len(sa | sb)
    cont = len(sa & sb) / max(min(len(sa), len(sb)), 2)   # a 1-word title is not "fully contained" in everything
    ca, cb = concepts(ta), concepts(tb)
    union = sum(cweight(c) for c in ca | cb)
    con = sum(cweight(c) for c in ca & cb) / union if union else 0.0
    other_a, other_b = sa - ca, sb - cb       # non-concept words (numbers count: "10x heavier" == "10x heavier")
    if not ((ca & cb) & STRONG) and not (other_a & other_b):
        con *= 0.5                            # only a generic concept in common ("magnet", "voice")
    seq = difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, " ".join(ta), " ".join(tb)).ratio()
    nums_a = {t for t in sa if re.match(r"^\d", t)}
    nums_b = {t for t in sb if re.match(r"^\d", t)}
    s = 0.40 * jac + 0.15 * cont + 0.25 * con + 0.20 * seq
    if not (personal(a) and personal(b)):     # "Earth's magnetic poles" is not a personal power
        s *= 0.8
    elif ca and ca == cb:                     # same core power, e.g. TIMESTOP vs TIMESTOP
        if (ca & STRONG) or (other_a & other_b) or (not other_a and not other_b):
            s = max(s, 0.62 + 0.2 * jac)
    if nums_a and nums_b and nums_a != nums_b and con > 0:
        s -= 0.05                             # 10x vs 1000x of the same power: related, not identical
    plain_a, plain_b = other_a - nums_a, other_b - nums_b
    if not ((ca & cb) & STRONG) and not (plain_a & plain_b) and (plain_a ^ plain_b):
        s = min(s, 0.7)                       # only "10x" + a generic concept shared ("Sleep 10x Faster" vs "10x Faster")
    return round(max(0.0, min(1.0, s)), 3)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- data
def load_lists():
    rows = []
    for f in sorted(COMP.glob("*.txt")):
        handle = f.stem
        for line in f.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines():
            parts = line.strip().split("|", 3)
            if len(parts) < 4 or not parts[3].strip():
                continue
            vid, dur, views, title = parts
            v = int(views) if views.isdigit() else None
            rows.append({"channel": handle, "id": vid, "dur": dur, "views": v, "title": title.strip()})
    return rows


def verdict(s):
    return "DUPLICATE" if s >= 0.8 else "CLOSE" if s >= 0.55 else "RELATED" if s >= 0.35 else "NOVEL"


def novelty_score(matches):
    """10 = nothing similar; 0 = exact premise already a hit. Penalise by the best match's views."""
    if not matches:
        return 10
    best = 10.0
    for m in matches[:5]:
        s, v = m["score"], m["views"] or 0
        if s < 0.35:
            cand = 10 - 3 * s
        elif s < 0.55:
            cand = 8 - 5 * (s - 0.35)
        elif s < 0.8:
            cand = 5.5 - 8 * (s - 0.55)
        else:
            cand = 2.5 - 5 * (s - 0.8)
        if s >= 0.55:
            cand -= 1.5 if v >= 100_000 else 0.75 if v >= 10_000 else 0
        best = min(best, cand)
    return max(0, round(best))


def check(title, premise="", top=8, rows=None):
    rows = rows if rows is not None else load_lists()
    scored = []
    for r in rows:
        s = similarity(title, r["title"])
        if premise:
            s = max(s, round(0.85 * similarity(premise, r["title"]), 3))
        if s > 0.2:
            scored.append({**r, "score": s, "verdict": verdict(s)})
    scored.sort(key=lambda r: (-r["score"], -(r["views"] or 0)))
    return {"title": title, "novelty": novelty_score(scored), "verdict": verdict(scored[0]["score"]) if scored else "NOVEL",
            "matches": scored[:top], "titles_checked": len(rows)}


def print_check(res):
    print(f"\n{res['title']}\n  novelty {res['novelty']}/10  verdict {res['verdict']}  (checked {res['titles_checked']} titles)")
    for m in res["matches"]:
        v = f"{m['views']:,}" if m["views"] else "?"
        print(f"   {m['score']:.2f} {m['verdict']:<9} {v:>11}  {m['channel']:<22} {m['title']}")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- refresh / search
def load_channels():
    if CHANNELS.exists():
        return json.loads(CHANNELS.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return {"channels": []}


def save_channels(cfg):
    CHANNELS.write_text(json.dumps(cfg, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")


def fetch(handle, timeout=240):
    url = f"https://www.youtube.com/@{handle}/videos"
    cmd = ["yt-dlp", "--flat-playlist", "--ignore-errors", "--no-warnings",
           "--print", "%(id)s|%(duration)s|%(view_count)s|%(title)s", url]
    try:
        p = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", timeout=timeout)
    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as e:
        return None, str(e)
    lines = [ln.strip() for ln in p.stdout.splitlines() if ln.count("|") >= 3]
    if not lines:
        return None, (p.stderr or "no output").strip()[:300]
    return lines, None


def refresh(handles):
    cfg = load_channels()
    known = {c["handle"]: c for c in cfg["channels"]}
    for h in handles:
        lines, err = fetch(h)
        if lines is None:
            print(f"  {h}: FAILED ({err})")
            continue
        (COMP / f"{h}.txt").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        c = known.setdefault(h, {"handle": h, "note": ""})
        c["videos"] = len(lines)
        c["refreshed"] = dt.date.today().isoformat()
        print(f"  {h}: {len(lines)} videos")
    cfg["channels"] = sorted(known.values(), key=lambda c: c["handle"].lower())
    save_channels(cfg)


def search(query, n):
    cmd = ["yt-dlp", "--flat-playlist", "--no-warnings", "--print",
           "%(channel)s|%(uploader_id)s|%(view_count)s|%(title)s", f"ytsearch{n}:{query}"]
    p = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", timeout=300)
    known = {c["handle"].lower() for c in load_channels()["channels"]}
    seen = {}
    for ln in p.stdout.splitlines():
        parts = ln.split("|", 3)
        if len(parts) < 4:
            continue
        ch, uid, views, title = parts
        h = uid.lstrip("@")
        seen.setdefault((ch, h), []).append((views, title))
    for (ch, h), vids in sorted(seen.items(), key=lambda kv: -len(kv[1])):
        tag = "known" if h.lower() in known else "NEW  "
        print(f"  {tag} @{h:<26} {ch[:28]:<28} {len(vids)} hit(s): {vids[0][1][:60]} ({vids[0][0]})")


def stats():
    rows = load_lists()
    by = {}
    for r in rows:
        by.setdefault(r["channel"], []).append(r)
    for ch, rs in sorted(by.items()):
        vs = [r["views"] for r in rs if r["views"]]
        med = statistics.median(vs) if vs else 0
        print(f"\n@{ch}: {len(rs)} videos, median views {med:,.0f}")
        for r in sorted([r for r in rs if r["views"]], key=lambda r: -r["views"])[:5]:
            print(f"   {r['views']:>11,} ({r['views'] / med if med else 0:4.1f}x)  {r['title']}")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- main
def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    c = sub.add_parser("check")
    c.add_argument("title")
    c.add_argument("--premise", default="")
    c.add_argument("--top", type=int, default=8)
    c.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    b = sub.add_parser("batch")
    b.add_argument("file")
    b.add_argument("--write", action="store_true", help="write novelty results back into the ideas file")
    b.add_argument("--top", type=int, default=3)
    r = sub.add_parser("refresh")
    r.add_argument("--channels", nargs="*")
    r.add_argument("--add", nargs="*", default=[])
    s = sub.add_parser("search")
    s.add_argument("query")
    s.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=30)
    sub.add_parser("stats")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    if a.cmd == "check":
        res = check(a.title, a.premise, a.top)
        print(json.dumps(res, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False) if a.json else "", end="")
        if not a.json:
            print_check(res)
    elif a.cmd == "batch":
        path = Path(a.file)
        data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        ideas = data["ideas"] if isinstance(data, dict) else data
        rows = load_lists()
        for idea in ideas:
            res = check(idea["title"], "", a.top, rows)
            print_check(res)
            if a.write:
                idea["novelty_check"] = {
                    "date": dt.date.today().isoformat(), "novelty": res["novelty"], "verdict": res["verdict"],
                    "closest": [{"title": m["title"], "channel": m["channel"], "views": m["views"], "score": m["score"]} for m in res["matches"][:a.top]],
                }
        if a.write:
            path.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
            print(f"\nwrote novelty_check into {path}")
    elif a.cmd == "refresh":
        cfg = load_channels()
        handles = a.channels if a.channels else [c["handle"] for c in cfg["channels"]]
        for h in a.add:
            if h not in handles:
                handles.append(h)
        refresh(handles)
    elif a.cmd == "search":
        search(a.query, a.n)
    elif a.cmd == "stats":
        stats()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
@@@@ END
@@@@ FILE tools/ideas/story_build/beat_stats.py | text | 8262 | e8c69d600dabf6b8ba5ad63d8df975aa85409b3cb3a7ee7a2ba92ce528ad0208
"""Join hand-annotated beats with transcript sentences + shot cuts; write data/story/beats/<id>.json.
Usage: python -I beat_stats.py <beats_src.json> <sents.json> <meta.json> <report.json> <out.json>
"""
import json, re, statistics as st, sys
from collections import defaultdict

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
src = json.load(open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8"))
sents = json.load(open(sys.argv[2], encoding="utf-8"))
meta = json.load(open(sys.argv[3], encoding="utf-8"))
rep = json.load(open(sys.argv[4], encoding="utf-8"))[src["id"]]
cuts = rep["cut_times"]
dur = float(meta["duration"])


def sec(x):
    if isinstance(x, (int, float)):
        return float(x)
    if not re.match(r"^\d+:\d\d$", x):
        return None
    m, s = x.split(":")
    return int(m) * 60 + int(s)


def fmt(t):
    return f"{int(t // 60)}:{int(round(t % 60)):02d}" if t is not None else None


WORD = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9][\w'’.,$-]*")
NUM = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z])(\d[\d,.]*)|\b(one|two|three|four|five|six|seven|eight|nine|ten|eleven|twelve|twenty|thirty|fifty|hundred|thousand|million|half|fifth|tenth|hundredth)\b", re.I)
for s in sents:
    s["w"] = len(WORD.findall(s["text"]))
    s["nums"] = len([m for m in NUM.finditer(s["text"]) if m.group(1)])

beats = src["beats"]
for b in beats:
    b["start"], b["end"] = sec(b["start"]), sec(b["end"])
for i, b in enumerate(beats):
    a, e = b["start"], b["end"]
    inb = [s for s in sents if a <= s["t"] < e]
    words = sum(s["w"] for s in inb)
    dlg = [s for s in inb if s.get("speaker")]
    # dialogue lines = runs of consecutive dialogue sentences with the same speaker
    lines, prev = 0, None
    for s in inb:
        k = s.get("speaker")
        if k and k != prev:
            lines += 1
        prev = k
    c = [t for t in cuts if a <= t < e]
    d = e - a
    b.update({
        "dur": round(d, 1),
        "words": words,
        "wpm": round(words / d * 60) if d > 0 else 0,
        "dialogue_words": sum(s["w"] for s in dlg),
        "dialogue_lines": lines,
        "cuts": len(c),
        "cuts_per_min": round(len(c) / d * 60, 1) if d > 0 else 0,
        "t": f"{fmt(a)}-{fmt(e)}",
        "pct": [round(100 * a / dur, 1), round(100 * e / dur, 1)],
    })

# --- video-level stats
words = sum(s["w"] for s in sents)
dlg_words = sum(s["w"] for s in sents if s.get("speaker"))
lines, prev = 0, None
for s in sents:
    k = s.get("speaker")
    if k and k != prev:
        lines += 1
    prev = k
by_type = defaultdict(lambda: {"count": 0, "total_s": 0.0})
for b in beats:
    by_type[b["beat"]]["count"] += 1
    by_type[b["beat"]]["total_s"] += b["dur"]
for k, v in by_type.items():
    v["total_s"] = round(v["total_s"], 1)
    v["pct_runtime"] = round(100 * v["total_s"] / dur, 1)


def intervals(ts):
    ts = sorted(ts)
    gaps = [b - a for a, b in zip(ts, ts[1:])]
    return {"count": len(ts), "mean_gap_s": round(st.mean(gaps), 1) if gaps else None,
            "median_gap_s": round(st.median(gaps), 1) if gaps else None,
            "max_gap_s": round(max(gaps), 1) if gaps else None}


acts = []
for a in src["acts"]:
    s0, e0 = sec(a["start"]), sec(a["end"])
    ab = [b for b in beats if b["act"] == a["act"]]
    c = [t for t in cuts if s0 <= t < e0]
    acts.append({"act": a["act"], "name": a["name"], "t": f"{fmt(s0)}-{fmt(e0)}",
                 "start_pct": round(100 * s0 / dur, 1), "end_pct": round(100 * e0 / dur, 1),
                 "dur_s": round(e0 - s0, 1), "beats": len(ab),
                 "words": sum(b["words"] for b in ab),
                 "cuts_per_min": round(len(c) / (e0 - s0) * 60, 1)})


def first(pred):
    for s in sents:
        if pred(s):
            return round(s["t"], 1)
    return None


txt_all = " ".join(s["text"] for s in sents)
quip_beats = [b for b in beats if b["quip"]]
comic = [b for b in beats if "comic_beat" in b["devices"] or "comic_callback" in b["devices"] or "comic_list" in b["devices"]]
turn_beats = ("but_turn", "real_problem", "reversal", "inciting_crisis", "dilemma", "reveal", "cliffhanger", "misuse", "tone_shift")
stats = {
    "duration_s": dur, "duration": fmt(dur),
    "views": meta.get("view_count"),
    "words": words, "wpm_runtime": round(words / dur * 60, 1),
    "dialogue_words": dlg_words, "dialogue_pct": round(100 * dlg_words / words, 1),
    "dialogue_lines": lines, "dialogue_lines_per_min": round(lines / dur * 60, 2),
    "seconds_per_dialogue_line": round(dur / max(lines, 1), 1),
    "sentences": len(sents), "avg_sentence_words": round(words / len(sents), 1),
    "questions": txt_all.count("?"), "questions_per_min": round(txt_all.count("?") / dur * 60, 2),
    "number_tokens": sum(s["nums"] for s in sents), "number_tokens_per_min": round(sum(s["nums"] for s in sents) / dur * 60, 2),
    "remember_count": len(re.findall(r"\bremember\b", txt_all, re.I)),
    "but_sentences": sum(1 for s in sents if re.match(r"^(But|but)\b", s["text"])),
    "title_question_s": first(lambda s: s["text"].lower().startswith("so, what if")),
    "first_number_s": first(lambda s: s["nums"] > 0),
    "first_but_turn_s": next((b["start"] for b in beats if b["beat"] == "but_turn" or (b["beat"] == "cost")), None),
    "beats": len(beats),
    "beat_mean_s": round(st.mean(b["dur"] for b in beats), 1),
    "beat_median_s": round(st.median(b["dur"] for b in beats), 1),
    "beat_types": dict(sorted(by_type.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]["total_s"])),
    "acts": acts,
    "new_info_cadence": intervals([b["start"] for b in beats if b["new_info"]]),
    "escalation_cadence": intervals([b["start"] for b in beats if b["escalation"]]),
    "turn_cadence": intervals([b["start"] for b in beats if b["beat"] in turn_beats]),
    "quip_beats": len(quip_beats), "quip_beats_per_min": round(len(quip_beats) / dur * 60, 2),
    "comic_beats": len(comic), "comic_beat_every_s": round(dur / max(len(comic), 1), 1),
    "cuts_total": len(cuts), "cuts_per_min": round(len(cuts) / dur * 60, 1), "avg_shot_s": round(dur / (len(cuts) + 1), 2),
    "words_per_shot": round(words / (len(cuts) + 1), 1),
    "top_cut_density_beats": [{"t": b["t"], "beat": b["beat"], "cuts_per_min": b["cuts_per_min"], "summary": b["summary"][:90]} for b in sorted([b for b in beats if b["dur"] >= 8], key=lambda b: -b["cuts_per_min"])[:6]],
    "top_spectacle_beats": [{"t": b["t"], "beat": b["beat"], "spectacle": b["spectacle"], "cuts_per_min": b["cuts_per_min"], "visual": b["visual"]} for b in sorted(beats, key=lambda b: (-b["spectacle"], -b["cuts_per_min"]))[:6]],
    "stakes_curve": [[b["t"], b["stakes"]] for b in beats],
    "open_loops": src.get("loops", []),
}
out = {
    "id": src["id"], "title": meta["title"], "channel": "IFOLOGY FILMS",
    "note": "Hand-annotated beats (summaries are paraphrases, not quotes). words/wpm/dialogue from deduplicated ASR sentences (data/story/transcripts); cuts from shot detection (research/sheets/report.json). spectacle = 1-5 judged from the 24-frame contact sheets + cut density + what the narration stages. Acts are analytic, not the creator's.",
    "fields": {"stakes": "1 comic/inconvenient .. 5 life/death or identity", "quip": "beat contains a short character line or punchline", "new_info": "beat introduces a new fact, rule, problem or plot information", "escalation": "beat raises scale or stakes vs the previous one"},
    "stats": stats,
    "beats": beats,
}
json.dump(out, open(sys.argv[5], "w", encoding="utf-8"), indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
print(src["id"], "words", words, "wpm", stats["wpm_runtime"], "lines", lines, "beats", len(beats), "cuts/min", stats["cuts_per_min"])
print("  acts", [(a["act"], a["t"], a["start_pct"]) for a in acts])
print("  new_info", stats["new_info_cadence"], "esc", stats["escalation_cadence"], "turns", stats["turn_cadence"])
print("  quip beats/min", stats["quip_beats_per_min"], "comic every", stats["comic_beat_every_s"], "dlg lines/min", stats["dialogue_lines_per_min"], "nums/min", stats["number_tokens_per_min"], "q/min", stats["questions_per_min"])
print("  top cuts", [(x["t"], x["beat"], x["cuts_per_min"]) for x in stats["top_cut_density_beats"]])
print("  title q", stats["title_question_s"], "first num", stats["first_number_s"])
print("  types", {k: (v["count"], v["total_s"]) for k, v in stats["beat_types"].items()})
@@@@ END
@@@@ FILE tools/ideas/story_build/build_transcript.py | text-crlf | 5512 | 780f7089315980435e830a24ad8d9dc6c0428a5636321dc95cfa24e6c8ca5e44
"""Deduped segments -> sentence list with timestamps + turn info + paragraphs markdown.
Usage: python -I build_transcript.py <segs.json> <meta.json> <overrides.json|-> <out_sent.json> <out.md>
overrides.json: {"dialogue": {"<sentence-prefix>": "Speaker"}, "narration": ["<sentence-prefix>", ...],
                 "fix": {"wrong text": "right text"}}
"""
import json, re, sys
sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
segs = json.load(open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8"))
meta = json.load(open(sys.argv[2], encoding="utf-8"))
ov = json.load(open(sys.argv[3], encoding="utf-8")) if sys.argv[3] != "-" else {}
fix = ov.get("fix", {})
TAGS = re.compile(r"\[(music|applause|laughter|Music|Applause|Laughter)\]")
# 1. word stream with interpolated times + turn markers
words = []  # (t, word, newturn)
for s in segs:
    txt = s["text"]
    newturn = txt.startswith(">>")
    txt = txt.replace(">>", " ")
    txt = TAGS.sub(" ", txt)
    toks = txt.split()
    if not toks:
        continue
    dur = max(s["end"] - s["start"], 0.3)
    for i, w in enumerate(toks):
        words.append([s["start"] + dur * i / len(toks), w, newturn and i == 0])
# 2. turns
turns, cur = [], []
for t, w, nt in words:
    if nt and cur:
        turns.append(cur); cur = []
    cur.append((t, w))
if cur: turns.append(cur)
# 3. sentences per turn
END = re.compile(r"[.?!]+[\"”']?$")
sents = []
for ti, turn in enumerate(turns):
    buf = []
    for j, (t, w) in enumerate(turn):
        buf.append((t, w))
        nxt = turn[j+1][1] if j+1 < len(turn) else None
        if END.search(w) and (nxt is None or nxt[0].isupper() or nxt[0].isdigit() or nxt[0] in "\"“"):
            # avoid splitting on decimals like 9.58 (handled since END requires terminal punct at token end)
            sents.append(dict(t=buf[0][0], text=" ".join(x[1] for x in buf), turn=ti, turn_words=len(turn)))
            buf = []
    if buf:
        sents.append(dict(t=buf[0][0], text=" ".join(x[1] for x in buf), turn=ti, turn_words=len(turn)))
for s in sents:
    for a, b in fix.items():
        s["text"] = s["text"].replace(a, b)
# 4. classify
dmap = ov.get("dialogue", {})
nlist = ov.get("narration", [])
for s in sents:
    spk = None
    def hit(key):
        pre, _, at = key.partition("@")
        return s["text"].startswith(pre) and (not at or abs(s["t"] - float(at)) < 10)
    for key, who in dmap.items():
        if hit(key):
            spk = who; break
    if spk is None and not any(hit(k) for k in nlist):
        if s["turn_words"] <= 14 and s["turn"] > 0:
            spk = "Character"
    s["speaker"] = spk
def fmt(t): return f"{int(t//60):02d}:{int(t%60):02d}"
# 5. paragraphs
TRANS = re.compile(r"^(So,|So |But |And then|Now,|Then |That night|The (first|second|third|fourth|fifth) (problem|rule)|Rule|Problem|For a while|Here's|And here's|One (day|morning|night|Saturday)|Years? later|Meanwhile|Months? later|Weeks? later|Next|Inside|Outside|By |At first)")
paras, curp = [], None
for s in sents:
    if s["speaker"]:
        if curp: paras.append(curp); curp = None
        paras.append(dict(t=s["t"], speaker=s["speaker"], text=s["text"]))
        continue
    if curp is None:
        curp = dict(t=s["t"], speaker=None, text=s["text"])
        continue
    age = s["t"] - curp["t"]
    if (age > 18 and TRANS.match(s["text"])) or age > 32:
        paras.append(curp); curp = dict(t=s["t"], speaker=None, text=s["text"])
    else:
        curp["text"] += " " + s["text"]
if curp: paras.append(curp)
# merge consecutive same-speaker dialogue lines
merged = []
for p in paras:
    if merged and p["speaker"] and merged[-1]["speaker"] == p["speaker"] and p["t"] - merged[-1]["t"] < 6:
        merged[-1]["text"] += " " + p["text"]
    else:
        merged.append(dict(p))
json.dump(sents, open(sys.argv[4], "w", encoding="utf-8"), indent=0, ensure_ascii=False)
nw = sum(len(re.findall(r"[A-Za-z0-9][\w'’.,-]*", s["text"])) for s in sents)
dw = sum(len(re.findall(r"[A-Za-z0-9][\w'’.,-]*", s["text"])) for s in sents if s["speaker"])
chap = meta.get("chapters") or []
ci = 0
with open(sys.argv[5], "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    fh.write(f"# {meta['title']} ({meta['id']})\n\n")
    fh.write(f"IFOLOGY FILMS. Duration {fmt(meta['duration'])}, {meta['view_count']:,} views at download. "
             f"Source: YouTube auto-captions (ASR), deduplicated and merged into sentences; [music] tags removed; "
             f"ASR misspellings kept unless obvious. ~{nw} spoken words, ~{dw} in character dialogue ({100*dw/max(nw,1):.0f}%).\n\n")
    fh.write("**Private local training data for pattern analysis only. Do not reuse lines in scripts.**\n\n")
    fh.write("Format: `[mm:ss]` paragraph start. Narrator (2nd person) is unmarked; character lines are `> **Speaker:** line`. "
             "Speaker attribution is inferred from ASR speaker-change marks and context, so treat it as approximate. "
             "`## ` headings are the creator's YouTube chapters.\n\n")
    for p in merged:
        while ci < len(chap) and chap[ci]["start_time"] <= p["t"] + 0.5:
            fh.write(f"\n## [{fmt(chap[ci]['start_time'])}] {chap[ci]['title']}\n\n"); ci += 1
        if p["speaker"]:
            fh.write(f"> **{p['speaker']}:** {p['text']}  \n\n")
        else:
            fh.write(f"[{fmt(p['t'])}] {p['text']}\n\n")
print(meta["id"], "sentences", len(sents), "words", nw, "dialogue words", dw, "paras", len(merged))
@@@@ END
@@@@ FILE tools/ideas/story_build/dedupe.py | text | 1404 | 2b7d893b07d555074e5da1f8f11c87628938d594b5290e864fa6ce2f7740943b
"""Rolling ASR SRT -> deduped segments [{start,end,text}] (text keeps '>>' speaker-change marks).
Usage: python -I dedupe.py <in.srt> <out.json> [<out.txt>]"""
import json, re, sys
sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
TS = r"(\d+):(\d\d):(\d\d)[.,](\d{3})"
def t2s(h, m, s, ms): return int(h)*3600 + int(m)*60 + int(s) + int(ms)/1000
raw = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read().replace("\r", "")
lines = raw.split("\n")
tsi = [(i, re.match(TS + r"\s*-->\s*" + TS, ln)) for i, ln in enumerate(lines)]
tsi = [(i, m) for i, m in tsi if m]
segs, prev = [], None
for k, (i, m) in enumerate(tsi):
    nxt = tsi[k+1][0] if k+1 < len(tsi) else len(lines)
    body = lines[i+1:nxt]
    if k+1 < len(tsi) and body and re.fullmatch(r"\d+", body[-1].strip()):
        body = body[:-1]
    g = m.groups(); st, en = t2s(*g[:4]), t2s(*g[4:])
    if en - st < 0.05: continue
    body = [l for l in body if l.strip()]
    if not body: continue
    last = body[-1].strip()
    if last == prev: continue
    prev = last
    segs.append(dict(start=round(st, 2), end=round(en, 2), text=last))
json.dump(segs, open(sys.argv[2], "w", encoding="utf-8"), indent=0, ensure_ascii=False)
if len(sys.argv) > 3:
    with open(sys.argv[3], "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for s in segs:
            fh.write(f"{int(s['start']//60)}:{int(s['start']%60):02d} {s['text']}\n")
print(len(segs), "segments")
@@@@ END

@@@@ FILE tools/pack/extract.mjs | text | 3042 | edf91797c15221e29d361039b049e8ffee3bdd126b32585cf0d0c993147815a6
// Unpacks "project instructions.md": writes every embedded file and checks its SHA-256.
//   node extract.mjs "<project instructions.md>" [outDir=.] [--memory <dir>] [--force]
// Files packed as @memory/… go to --memory (Claude's memory folder), or to .bootstrap/memory/ without it.
// An existing file that differs is kept unless --force. Exit 1 if any checksum fails.
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import crypto from 'node:crypto';

const args = process.argv.slice(2);
const take = k => { const i = args.indexOf(k); return i < 0 ? undefined : args.splice(i, 2)[1]; };
const memDir = take('--memory');
const force = args.includes('--force');
const [src, outDir = '.'] = args.filter(a => a !== '--force');
if (!src) {
  console.error('usage: node extract.mjs "<project instructions.md>" [outDir] [--memory <dir>] [--force]');
  process.exit(2);
}

const lines = fs.readFileSync(src, 'utf8').replace(/\r\n/g, '\n').split('\n');
const sha = b => crypto.createHash('sha256').update(b).digest('hex');
const HEAD = /^@@@@ FILE (.+) \| (text|text-crlf|base64) \| (\d+) \| ([0-9a-f]{64})( \| noeol)?$/;
let i = lines.indexOf('@@@@ PAYLOAD BEGIN');
if (i < 0) throw new Error('no payload found in ' + src);
const n = { written: 0, same: 0, dirs: 0, kept: [], bad: [] };
for (i++; i < lines.length && lines[i] !== '@@@@ PAYLOAD END'; i++) {
  const line = lines[i];
  if (line.startsWith('@@@@ DIR ')) {
    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(outDir, line.slice(9)), { recursive: true });
    n.dirs++;
    continue;
  }
  const m = HEAD.exec(line);
  if (!m) {
    if (line.trim()) throw new Error(`line ${i + 1}: expected a FILE header, got: ${line.slice(0, 80)}`);
    continue;
  }
  const [, rel, enc, size, hash, noeol] = m;
  const body = [];
  for (i++; lines[i] !== '@@@@ END'; i++) {
    if (i >= lines.length) throw new Error('unterminated entry: ' + rel);
    body.push(lines[i]);
  }
  let buf;
  if (enc === 'base64') buf = Buffer.from(body.join(''), 'base64');
  else {
    let t = body.join('\n') + (noeol ? '' : '\n');
    if (enc === 'text-crlf') t = t.replace(/\n/g, '\r\n');
    buf = Buffer.from(t, 'utf8');
  }
  if (buf.length !== +size || sha(buf) !== hash) {
    n.bad.push(rel);
    continue;
  }
  const dst = rel.startsWith('@memory/')
    ? path.join(memDir ?? path.join(outDir, '.bootstrap', 'memory'), rel.slice(8))
    : path.join(outDir, rel);
  if (fs.existsSync(dst)) {
    if (sha(fs.readFileSync(dst)) === hash) { n.same++; continue; }
    if (!force) { n.kept.push(rel); continue; }
  }
  fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(dst), { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(dst, buf);
  n.written++;
}
console.log(`${n.written} files written, ${n.same} already identical, ${n.dirs} folders, ${n.bad.length} checksum failures`);
if (n.kept.length) console.log(`kept ${n.kept.length} existing files that differ (pass --force to overwrite):\n  ${n.kept.join('\n  ')}`);
if (n.bad.length) {
  console.error(`CHECKSUM FAILED (this file was altered after packing):\n  ${n.bad.join('\n  ')}`);
  process.exit(1);
}
@@@@ END
@@@@ FILE tools/pack/fresh/ELEVENLABS_SETUP.md | text | 4039 | 013b4b6053f7dc6d007e6255040d5cfd346468eea0a0a4b05df699429c08775b
# ElevenLabs: first-connect checklist

Voice (narration + character lines) uses the ElevenLabs API, called directly with `fetch` from `tools/episode.mjs` — no MCP. Run this checklist once, the first time a copy of this project has no working `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`.

Until the key is working, everything except real voice-over works: ideas, scripts, shot lists, `draft` previews, short shots with Python sound, audits, reviews and preview renders. If the user asks for a finished episode before the key works, go up to the preview (docs/pipeline/EPISODE.md step 4), then ask them for a key.

## Choices made at setup

- Narrator voice: default pick for the content language, chosen at setup — run step 3 now and confirm the pick, unless the setup answer was "audition first", in which case run step 3 as a full audition before picking anything

## Steps

1. **Get a key.** Ask the user for their ElevenLabs API key (elevenlabs.io/app/settings/api-keys → Create API Key). Save it to `.env` at the project root as `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=...` (the `.env` file is gitignored — never commit it or print it back in full).

2. **Smoke test.** `GET https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/voices` (header `xi-api-key: <key>`) must return 200. If it 401s, the key is wrong; if it 403s with `missing_permissions`, the key is scoped — note which permissions are missing (voices/TTS access is enough to run the pipeline; `user_read` is only needed for an automatic balance check, see step 5).

3. **Pick house voices.** `tools/episode.mjs`'s `HOUSE_VOICES` needs a narrator, a male and a female voice, in the project's content language. The account's own saved voices (`/v1/voices`) may not have what's needed — search the full public library instead:
   - `GET /v1/shared-voices?language=<lang>&use_cases=narrative_story` for narrator candidates (calm/warm, not "excited" or "upbeat" — the house style is unhurried).
   - `GET /v1/shared-voices?language=<lang>&gender=male` / `&gender=female` for the secondary voices (young, casual/natural).
   - Pull 3–4 candidates per role, fetch each one's `preview_url`, and let the user pick by ear — don't choose a voice the user hasn't heard.
   - A public-library voice_id can be used directly in a TTS call without first "adding" it to the account.

4. **Measure the real cost before committing.** Credit cost per character varies by model and isn't published cleanly — measure it: call `POST /v1/text-to-speech/{voice_id}/with-timestamps` with a short (~15 s) test script in the project's content language and the chosen narrator voice and model (`eleven_v4` unless the user asks otherwise), then diff `GET /v1/usage/character-stats?start_unix=<ms>&end_unix=<ms>&include_live_requests=true` before/after (its `usage.All` series updates within a few seconds). Report the measured credits/char to the user and update the `CREDITS_PER_CHAR` constant and the Voice section of `docs/pipeline/EPISODE.md`.

5. **Balance checks.** `GET /v1/user/subscription` gives the real remaining balance, but needs the `user_read` permission. If the key doesn't have it, tell the user to check elevenlabs.io/app/subscription manually, or to create a key with that permission added, before any `/stickman` credit checkpoint.

6. **Finish.**
   - Update `HOUSE_VOICES` in `tools/episode.mjs`, the **Voice** section of `docs/pipeline/EPISODE.md`, and `public/episodes/pipetest/episode.json` (`voice.id`) if it exists.
   - Replace the memory file `project-elevenlabs-pending.md` with a short `reference` memory: "ElevenLabs connected `<date>`, narrator `<voice>`, measured `<rate>` credits/char." Update its line in `MEMORY.md`.
   - Tell the user what was checked, which voices were picked, and the measured cost.

## Costs to keep in mind

- Voice: credits/char varies by model — don't assume 1:1. See step 4 for how to measure it for real.
- Re-running `node tools/episode.mjs sections <slug>` is free; only `node tools/episode.mjs voice <slug>` spends credits, and only for sections that don't already have a `file`.
@@@@ END
@@@@ FILE tools/pack/fresh/FISH_SETUP.md | text | 2324 | 64d29f02c68b5751e17b59b8d1fea53be61f5afb3e75b1b1b525bb73f63c0e5d
# Fish Audio: thumbnail-mode first-connect checklist

Fish Audio is used only for `fish`-mode thumbnail image generation (GPT Image 2.5 via Fish's media API) — see docs/pipeline/EPISODE.md step 10. Voice does not use Fish; see `docs/ELEVENLABS_SETUP.md` for that.

Run this checklist once, the first time Fish tools are available in a session, if the thumbnail mode is `fish`. Their tool names end in `get_media_model`, `list_media_models`, `create_media_upload`, `get_credit_balance`, `list_my_workspaces`. If they appear only as deferred tools, load them with ToolSearch first.

Run this checklist again whenever the Fish account changes: the thumbnail reference keys must be reachable from the connected team.

## Choices made at setup

- Thumbnails: `fish` mode (the default) — run steps 1–2 now

## Steps

1. **Thumbnail model.**
   1. Call `get_media_model` with the `model_id` in `thumbnails/config.json` (`gpt-image-2.5-flare`).
   2. Check that it accepts the `parameters` there (16:9, 2K, medium) and `ref` image inputs, and keep its `parameter_schema`.
   3. If the model is gone or renamed, call `list_media_models`, propose the closest GPT Image model, and ask before you change `config.json`.

2. **Thumbnail references.** The `object_key`s in `thumbnails/refs/refs.json` belong to the Fish workspace the project was packed from, so upload the three images again, in order. Uploads are free.
   1. `list_my_workspaces` gives the `workspace_id`.
   2. For each `thumbnails/refs/<file>`, call `create_media_upload` with `file_name` (`ref1_paused.webp`, etc.), the exact byte size and `image/webp`.
   3. PUT the file to the returned `upload_url`: `curl.exe -X PUT -H "Content-Type: image/webp" --data-binary "@thumbnails/refs/<file>" "<upload_url>"`.
   4. Write each new `object_key` into `refs.json`, keeping the order, and set `uploaded` to today's date.

3. **Finish.**
   - Add "Last run: <date>, team <name>" under the title of this file and keep the file, for the next account change.
   - Tell the user what was checked, what changed, and what it cost.

## Costs to keep in mind

- Thumbnails (`fish` mode): 1,601 credits per 2K variant, so 3 variants are about 4.8k per episode.
- Fish AI video models are not used for episodes. A clip costs 1.4k–53k credits, and the procedural engine is free.

@@@@ FILE tools/pack/fresh/stickman.md | text | 5097 | fc0b77a39e80884eea318d5ca042d4b0fcbcc7469d4f19f6ed61bb53196f011e
---
description: Make a full "What If" stickman episode from a topic, then generate its 3 thumbnails
argument-hint: <video topic, e.g. What If You Could Swap Places With Anyone>
---

# /stickman: topic → finished video + 3 thumbnails

Topic: **$ARGUMENTS**

If the topic is empty, ask for one and stop.

Make one complete narrated episode about this topic with the saved hero, then generate its 3 thumbnails. Follow `docs/pipeline/EPISODE.md` (the long-form pipeline, moved out of CLAUDE.md) step by step; this command only fixes the choices below. Keep a task list for the whole run.

## Fixed choices

- **Hero:** the saved character, the `hero` entry in `src/cast.ts`, exactly as it is. Don't change the outfit, and keep its signature colour off everyone else (CLAUDE.md, "… belongs to the hero").
- **Idea:** the topic replaces the idea step. Skip candidate generation and pitching. Shape it into a "What If" title (keep the user's wording when it already is one), run `python -I tools/ideas/novelty.py "<title>"`, and mention any close competitor title in the summary.
- **Slug:** short kebab-case from the title, not already used in `public/episodes/`.
- **Length:** at least 10:00 of voiced narration (user rule, 2026-11-09); the audit warns below that. Write ~1,600–1,700 PT-BR words, since the paced read runs ~175 wpm.
- **Voice, music, look:** the house defaults in `docs/pipeline/EPISODE.md` and memory.
- **Tone:** acid, bold and still monetizable, never the cute family tone: a narrator who is calm but sometimes malicious or sarcastic (`STORY_BLUEPRINT.md` §6.10, summarised in the cola's "Tom" section).
- **Pacing:** the generator calls `episode(..., ritmo='rapido')`, as `_modelo.py` does. That gives automatic sub-cuts plus whip/zoom on set changes. Use `coverage='calm'` in the dilemma and `cut='smash'` by hand on reveals. Keep the subject and key text in the 9:16 centre column (audit `vertical`).
- **Shorts:** at least 4 self-contained ~90 s clips, marked in `episode(clips=[...])` (cola, "Cortes para shorts"). The user cuts them by hand from the 16:9, so there is no vertical render.

## Run

1. **Script** (`docs/story/COLA_ROTEIRO.md`; open `STORY_BLUEPRINT.md` only at the § it names): beat sheet, script, plant ledger, fact check and score in `script_notes.md`.
2. **Shot list:** `episode.json`, generated from `tools/episodes/<slug>.py` (copy `_modelo.py`; helpers in `kit.py`), then `node tools/episode.mjs draft <slug>`, `npm test`, `node tools/qa.cjs audit <slug>` and `node tools/episode.mjs check <slug>` (vo text: tags, SSML, raw numbers — EPISODE.md step 5.0). Fix every error, then self-certify STORY_BLUEPRINT.md §9's "Tags de áudio e fala" group by eye — `check` is mechanical and won't catch a misplaced or mismatched tag.
3. **One checkpoint before spending credits.** Check the ElevenLabs credit balance (`GET /v1/user/subscription`; if the API key lacks `user_read`, ask the user to check elevenlabs.io/app/subscription or widen the key) and show the user, in one message:
   - the title and a short synopsis;
   - the script score and the path to `script.md`;
   - the credit estimate: voice (`node tools/episode.mjs sections <slug>` prints it, ~0.4 credits/char on eleven_v4 — see the Voice section of EPISODE.md) plus thumbnails (3 × the per-image cost in `thumbnails/config.json`, fish mode only).

   Wait for one OK. That OK covers the voice and the 3 thumbnails; don't ask again for either. If the balance is too low, say so and stop there.
4. **Voice, align, pre-render review:** EPISODE.md steps 5–7, including the independent reviewer rounds (round 1 on the `revisor-episodio` agent, round 2+ on `revisor-verificacao`). Build only on "ready for final render".
5. **Build and check:** steps 8–9. Re-render broken ranges until the sheets are clean.
6. **Thumbnails:** step 10, with the video now finished:
   - write `thumbnails/<slug>/brief.json` with exactly 3 variants (one scene per variant, drawn from the episode's strongest moments), then `node tools/thumb-prompt.mjs <slug>`;
   - `fish` mode: run `estimate_image_edit`, then submit all 3 jobs (already approved at the checkpoint), poll them together, and save each to `thumbnails/<slug>/out/<id>_2k_medium.png`. Review each at full size and at ~360 px; regenerate one only if it fails the step-10 checks (spelling, hero colour, stickman-only cast, no stray text), and only within the approved credits;
   - `chatgpt` mode: send `CHATGPT.md` and the three prompt files instead.
7. **Update `final/README.md`** with the new episode row (create it if missing, e.g. on a fresh clone).

## Deliver

Keep the final message short:
1. send the video, `final/<Episode title>.mp4`, with SendUserFile (`display: "render"`);
2. send the 3 thumbnails with SendUserFile in one call, captioned A / B / C with their text;
3. one or two lines: title, length, the 4+ clip timecodes from `final/<title> - cortes.txt` (the `.srt` beside the video is for the user's editor), and any warning you accepted. Ask which thumbnail to pick (`node tools/thumb-prompt.mjs <slug> --pick <id>`).
@@@@ END

# Project instructions: 3D Stickman Long

**Claude: read only lines 1–{{HEADER_END}} of this file.** Everything after that is the packed project ({{SIZE_MB}} MB). If the user typed **start**, follow "For Claude: what start means" below.

This one file rebuilds the 3D Stickman Long production system in an empty folder. That system makes IFOLOGY-style "What If" videos with a 3D stickman hero, built in code with Remotion 4 and Three.js, with Python sound effects and ElevenLabs narration. The file holds:
- the engine, sets, cards and overlays;
- every tool;
- the style, story and research docs and the idea-engine data;
- the thumbnail template and reference images;
- Claude's project memory;
- the `/stickman <topic>` command (topic in, finished video and 3 thumbnails out).

It holds {{FILE_COUNT}} files in all, each with a checksum. It was packed on {{DATE}}. It holds no finished videos or episodes: you start with an empty channel.

## For the human

1. Make an empty folder and put this file in it. Keep the name `project instructions.md`.
2. Open a new Claude Code chat on that folder: the Code tab of the desktop app, or `claude` in a terminal there.
3. Type **start**. (If Claude asks what to start, say "follow project instructions.md".)

At {{SIZE_MB}} MB, the file is too big to paste into a chat, so it has to sit in the folder.

Claude asks four setup questions first:
- what the main character wears (with ready-made looks if you don't want to describe one);
- what language scripts, narration and overlays are written in;
- the narrator voice;
- how thumbnails are made.

Then it installs and checks everything. That takes 5–20 minutes depending on your connection (npm downloads about 1.5 GB) and on how much the outfit changes.

You need Windows 10 or 11, a GPU, and about 4 GB of free disk. Claude installs Node, Python and ffmpeg with winget if they're missing, after asking you.

**ElevenLabs** (voice) is connected afterwards:
1. Get an API key at elevenlabs.io/app/settings/api-keys.
2. Open a new chat in the project folder and give Claude the key.
3. Claude runs `docs/ELEVENLABS_SETUP.md`: it saves the key to `.env`, picks house voices in your language, and measures the real credit cost.

**Fish Audio** is separate and optional — only needed if you picked `fish`-mode thumbnails:
1. Add the Fish Audio connector to your Claude account, or the Fish Audio MCP server to Claude Code.
2. Open a new chat in the project folder and say "Fish is connected".
3. Claude runs `docs/FISH_SETUP.md`: it checks the thumbnail model and uploads the reference images.

Everything else works before either is connected: ideas, scripts, shot lists, previews and short shots.

## For Claude: what "start" means

You are installing an existing project from this file. Every project file comes out of the payload, byte for byte, with its checksum verified. Never write a project file from memory or "improve" one while installing. The only edits you make are the ones the setup answers call for (step 7).

Never read past line {{HEADER_END}} with Read, cat or grep: the rest is {{SIZE_MB}} MB of payload. Keep a task list, and run the long installs in the background.

**Shell.** Run every command in the Bash tool (Git Bash), with forward slashes, exactly as written here: `.venv/Scripts/python`, `--props='{"view":"close"}'`. If there is no Bash tool, use PowerShell:
- write `.venv\Scripts\python`;
- pass `--props` as the path of a small JSON file (`--props=out/lab/close.json`), because PowerShell 5.1 strips the inner quotes of inline JSON;
- write the extractor with the Write tool (step 4).

### 1. Look before you start

- The folder should contain only this file, plus `.bootstrap/` if an earlier attempt stopped. If it holds other files, tell the user and ask before going on. The extractor never overwrites a file that differs unless you pass `--force`.
- Note whether the user has already mentioned an ElevenLabs API key, and whether Fish Audio tools are already available in this session (names ending in `get_credit_balance`, `get_media_model`, …, loaded or deferred). You need both in step 9.

### 2. Ask the setup questions

Ask all four in **one** AskUserQuestion call. If the tool isn't available, ask in chat and wait.

1. Header "Outfit". Question: "What should the main character wear?"
   - **Red hoodie (Recommended)**: "The original look: red hoodie with coral trim and white drawstrings, dark purple joggers, light sneakers."
   - **Purple hoodie**: "The channel's first look: purple hoodie with lilac trim, dark joggers, light sneakers."
   - **Orange hoodie + headband**: "Bright orange hoodie with cream trim, a white sweatband, charcoal joggers, white sneakers."
   - **Yellow bomber + cap**: "Sporty: yellow bomber jacket with charcoal trim, a cream cap, charcoal pants, white sneakers."
   - The automatic "Other" option lets the user describe their own outfit.
2. Header "Language". Question: "What language should scripts, narration, overlays and thumbnails be written in?"
   - **English (Recommended)**: "The language the engine's docs and example scripts are written in."
   - **Portuguese (PT-BR)**: "Scripts, VO text, overlays and thumbnail text in Portuguese. Code, docs and comments stay in English."
   - The automatic "Other" option lets the user name any other language; the story docs (`STORY_BLUEPRINT.md`, `COLA_ROTEIRO.md`, `IDEA_ENGINE.md`, `script_analysis.md`) get translated the same way.
3. Header "Narrator". Question: "Which narrator voice should ElevenLabs use once it's connected?"
   - **Default for the chosen language (Recommended)**: "Claude picks a calm, warm narrator in that language from ElevenLabs' public voice library once connected, and confirms it with you by ear before locking it in."
   - **Audition first**: "When ElevenLabs is connected, Claude plays you free samples of 3–4 narrators in that language and you pick."
4. Header "Thumbnails". Question: "How should thumbnails be made?"
   - **Fish GPT Image (Recommended)**: "Claude generates 3 options at 2K through Fish once it's connected (about 4.8k credits per episode)."
   - **ChatGPT, by hand**: "Free: Claude writes the prompts, you paste them into ChatGPT with the 3 reference images."

There is deliberately no blue option. The lead of IFOLOGY FILMS, the channel this style is modelled on, wears a blue hoodie, and the thumbnail reference images show him in it. A blue hoodie would read as a copy of that character. If the user describes a blue hoodie under "Other", tell them this and suggest another colour; go ahead only if they insist.

### 3. Check the prerequisites

Check each of these:
- `node --version`: 20 or newer (the original used v24.16.0);
- Python 3.11 or newer (`py -3.14 --version`, `py --version` or `python --version`; the original used 3.14.3);
- `ffmpeg -version` and `ffprobe -version`;
- optional: `yt-dlp --version`, which `tools/ideas/novelty.py refresh` uses to update competitor titles.

If something is missing, ask once, then install it with winget:
- `winget install -e --id OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS`
- `winget install -e --id Python.Python.3.14`
- `winget install -e --id Gyan.FFmpeg`
- `winget install -e --id yt-dlp.yt-dlp`

A new install isn't on PATH until a new shell starts. Find the full path, for example under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WinGet\Packages\`, or ask the user to restart the app and type start again; this procedure picks up where it left off. If winget itself is missing, give the user the download pages and wait.

### 4. Unpack

1. Copy the extractor below into `.bootstrap/extract.mjs` exactly as written.
   - In Bash, run this from the project folder; it copies the file exactly:
     `mkdir -p .bootstrap && awk '/^```js extract\.mjs$/{f=1;next} f&&/^```$/{exit} f' "project instructions.md" > .bootstrap/extract.mjs`
   - Without Bash, write it with the Write tool.
2. Run it:

```
node .bootstrap/extract.mjs "project instructions.md" . --memory "<memory folder>"
```

`<memory folder>` is the persistent memory directory that your system prompt names, such as `C:\Users\<name>\.claude\projects\<folder>\memory`. If your system prompt names none, use `docs/memory`. After the extractor has run, add this line directly under the title of `CLAUDE.md`, above the ElevenLabs note, unless it's already there:

`Project memory (the user's preferences and decisions) lives in docs/memory/: read MEMORY.md and the files it links at the start of every session, and save new memories there.`

The extractor must print `0 checksum failures`. If any file fails, this file was changed after packing (an editor or a transfer altered it). Ask the user for a fresh copy. Never hand-write the missing files.

```js extract.mjs
{{EXTRACTOR}}
```

3. Read `CLAUDE.md`, `HOW_TO_USE.md`, `docs/STYLE.md` and the memory files now. They are the project's rules. This session started before they existed, so none of them is loaded yet. From here on, follow them as any session in this project would.

   They record the decisions of the person who built the system: dates, the `swap-pilot` episode, credit balances. Treat them as the house rules and history of this project. The swap-pilot episode itself isn't included; only its thumbnail brief ships, as the example format.

**Editing files.** Many files use CRLF line endings. Keep each file's endings as they are:
- the Edit tool does this;
- `sed -i` in Git Bash silently converts a file to LF;
- Python's `write_text` on Windows forces CRLF.

### 5. Install

1. Run `npm ci` in the background. It installs the exact versions in `package-lock.json`, about 1.5 GB.
   - npm reports some "high severity vulnerabilities" in dependencies. That is expected.
   - Don't run `npm audit fix`: it changes the pinned versions.
2. Run `npx remotion browser ensure`. It downloads the headless Chrome that Remotion renders with.
3. Create the Python environment at the project root. The build tools call `.venv/Scripts/python.exe`, so it must live there.
   - Run `py -3.14 -m venv .venv`, or use whichever Python 3.11+ you found.
   - Then run `.venv/Scripts/python -m pip install numpy==2.5.4 scipy==1.18.1`.
   - If those exact versions have no wheel for that Python, install the latest `numpy scipy` and say so in the report.
4. Run `.venv/Scripts/python -I tools/sfx/pill_sprint.py`. This writes `public/audio/pill_sprint_mix.wav`, the soundtrack of the `PillSprint` reference composition. Without it, that composition fails to load in the studio.

`episode.mjs align` needs no local model — it reads timestamps ElevenLabs already returned, so there's nothing to download here.

### 6. Run the gates

All of these must pass:
- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm test`: every engine self-test prints PASS.
- `node tools/qa.cjs audit pipetest`: 0 errors. `pipetest` is the small fixture episode the compositions default to. It has no audio, which is expected. One framing warning (feet out of frame) is also expected.

### 7. Apply the setup answers

#### Outfit

As packed, the `hero` entry in `src/cast.ts` is:

`{{HERO_ENTRY}}`

If the chosen look is that one, skip to "Narrator". Otherwise work through these six steps. Below, "the old outfit" and "the old colour" mean this packed look.

1. **The hero.** Set the `hero` entry in `src/cast.ts`. The fields are `Outfit` in `src/types.ts`:
   - `top`: hoodie, jacket, tee, coat, dress or suit, with `topColor` and `accent` (trim, drawstrings, zip);
   - `bottom`: pants, shorts or skirt, with `bottomColor`;
   - `shoes`;
   - optional `hat` (cap, headband or helmet) with `hatColor`, and `glasses`;
   - `hair`: keep `none`, the IFOLOGY look, unless the user asked for hair.

   | Look | `hero` entry (after `name: 'Hero'`) |
   |---|---|
   | Red hoodie | `top: 'hoodie', topColor: '#d1342b', accent: '#ff9a8b', bottom: 'pants', bottomColor: '#38275e', shoes: '#efe8ff', hair: 'none'` |
   | Purple hoodie | `top: 'hoodie', topColor: '#7b4fd0', accent: '#c9b2ff', bottom: 'pants', bottomColor: '#2b2540', shoes: '#efe8ff', hair: 'none'` |
   | Orange hoodie + headband | `top: 'hoodie', topColor: '#f07a1f', accent: '#ffe2c2', bottom: 'pants', bottomColor: '#34343c', shoes: '#ffffff', hat: 'headband', hatColor: '#f4f1ea', hair: 'none'` |
   | Yellow bomber + cap | `top: 'jacket', topColor: '#f2c230', accent: '#2b2f3a', bottom: 'pants', bottomColor: '#2b2f3a', shoes: '#ffffff', hat: 'cap', hatColor: '#f4f1ea', hair: 'none'` |

   For an outfit of the user's own, map it onto these fields.
   - Keep hats light-coloured: a dark hat vanishes into the black head.
   - Avoid `hat: 'beanie'`. It renders as a bare dome that reads as a grey helmet. Offer a cap or headband instead, or give the beanie a rolled cuff first: a `memo()`'d LatheGeometry with points bottom → top.
   - A piece the engine doesn't have (a cape, a scarf): use the nearest supported look and tell the user. Build it only if it's small, in `src/engine/Stickman.tsx`, following CLAUDE.md's hard-won rules.
   - Ask a follow-up question only if the description can't be used at all.

2. **The signature colour belongs to the hero.** The outfit's main colour becomes the hero's, and nobody else may wear it. Judge by eye at thumbnail size (~360 px wide), not by hex.
   - These count as the same hue: navy as blue; coral and maroon as red; lilac, violet and periwinkle as purple; amber as orange; gold and mustard as yellow.
   - Pink and magenta are not purple, and teal is not blue or green.
   - If you're unsure, recolour it.

   Recolour every match in the places that dress people or carry team colours:
   - `src/cast.ts`: every other character and the extras, including accents, hats and shoes;
   - `src/sets/kit.tsx`: the crowd `shirts`, which several outdoor sets use;
   - `src/sets/classroom.tsx`: `SHIRTS` (the cafeteria uses them too);
   - `src/sets/stadium.tsx`:
     - the team colours `HOME`/`AWAY` (they also paint end zones, benches and the scoreboard roof);
     - the crowd `SHIRTS`;
     - the scoreboard `Sign` backgrounds;
     - the midfield logo;
     - `BOARD_BG` and `BOARD_TEXT` (the background and the words, e.g. a "PURPLE PRIDE" board for a purple hero).

   Pick replacements that are neither the new signature colour nor the old one, so neither competes with the hero. Leave every colour that doesn't clash as it is.

   Environment colours (walls, chairs, roofs, cabinets) and effect colours (power glows, aura, ghosts) don't count. But check the sets whose environment shares the new colour (purple: the home kitchen's cabinets, the suburb's roofs). Render each one with the hero in it (`"hero":"hero"` in the SetLab props), and tell the user what clashes, rather than repainting the set.

For a jacket, the `hoodie` object describes the jacket; its key names may stay. Add the hat if there is one.

#### Language

If the answer was "English", change nothing.

Otherwise (Portuguese or another language):
- Add a line near the top of `CLAUDE.md`, right after the outfit paragraph: "**Scripts, shot-list `vo` text, overlays and thumbnail text are written in <language>** as of <date> (chosen at setup). - Translate `docs/story/STORY_BLUEPRINT.md`, `docs/story/IDEA_ENGINE.md` and `docs/research/script_analysis.md` into that language: prose, checklists and example script lines (rewritten as a native speaker would write that same beat, not translated word-for-word), but not JSON field names, file paths, commands or code. If a pacing number in those docs (words per minute, syllables, characters per line) looks English-specific, leave the number as-is and tell the user it may need a human recheck for the new language — don't invent a new number yourself.
- Add a dated line to `project-pt-br-adaptation.md` (name it for the actual language if not Portuguese) recording the choice, under memory type `project`, and a line in `MEMORY.md`.

#### Narrator

If the answer was "Audition first":
- in `docs/ELEVENLABS_SETUP.md`, change the "Narrator voice" line under "Choices made at setup" to "audition requested at setup: run step 3 as a full audition before picking anything";
- add a dated line to `project-narrator-voice.md`: the user asked to audition narrators once ElevenLabs is connected, with no default locked in until they pick.

Otherwise change nothing — step 9 picks a default once ElevenLabs is connected and confirms it with the user.

#### Thumbnails

If the answer was "ChatGPT, by hand":
- in `thumbnails/config.json`, set `"mode": "chatgpt"`;
- in `docs/pipeline/EPISODE.md` step 10, change "(current: `fish`)" to "(current: `chatgpt`)";
- in `project-thumbnails-gpt-image.md`, change "Mode stays `fish` for now" to "Mode is `chatgpt` (chosen at setup, <date>)";
- in `MEMORY.md`, change "(fish now)" to "(chatgpt now)";
- in `docs/FISH_SETUP.md`, change the "Thumbnails" line to "`chatgpt` mode, chosen at setup: skip steps 5–6 unless the user switches to `fish`".

Otherwise change nothing.

### 8. Final look

If the outfit didn't change, render `out/lab/hero_close.png` and the two lineups from step 7 now, and look at all three. This proves the GPU render path works on this machine. If step 7 already rendered them after its last edit, they serve.

### 9. ElevenLabs and Fish Audio

The unpacked `CLAUDE.md` starts with an "ElevenLabs is not connected yet" note, and the memory has `project-elevenlabs-pending.md` (and `project-fish-pending.md`, for `fish`-mode thumbnails only). Together they make every later session run the matching setup doc the first time it can.
- If the user already gave an API key (from step 1), run `docs/ELEVENLABS_SETUP.md` now: save the key to `.env`, pick house voices in the chosen language (step 3 there), and measure the real credit cost. Ask before anything that spends credits.
- If Fish tools are already available in this session and the thumbnail answer was `fish`, also run `docs/FISH_SETUP.md` now.
- Otherwise leave the pending notes and memories in place.

### 10. Finish

Delete `.bootstrap/`. Leave `project instructions.md` where it is: it's this copy's installer, and `node tools/pack/pack.mjs` refreshes it after changes.

Report to the user:
- files unpacked, and the checksum result;
- what was installed, with versions;
- the gate results;
- the outfit applied, every colour you moved off the cast, and `hero_close.png` and `lineup_a.png` sent by SendUserFile;
- the language, narrator and thumbnail choices;
- anything that failed or was skipped.

End with how to connect ElevenLabs (get a key, give it to Claude in a new chat) and, if the thumbnail answer was `fish`, how to connect Fish Audio too (connect it, open a new chat here, say "Fish is connected") — plus two or three things to ask for next, from `HOW_TO_USE.md`, such as "Give me 3 new What If ideas" or `/stickman What If You Could Breathe Underwater`. Mention that `/stickman` shows up in a new chat (commands load when a session starts).

// Packs the production system into "project instructions.md": one file that rebuilds it in an empty folder
// when the user types "start" in a fresh Claude Code chat. It holds the start procedure (tools/pack/header.md),
// the extractor (tools/pack/extract.mjs) and every source, doc and data file plus Claude's project memory,
// verbatim or base64, each with its SHA-256. No videos, episodes or render outputs: the copy starts as an empty
// channel, set up before ElevenLabs (voice) and Fish Audio (optional, fish-mode thumbnails only) are connected
// (tools/pack/fresh/ adds the first-connect checklists and notes for both).
//   node tools/pack/pack.mjs [--out <file>] [--memory <dir>]
import fs from 'node:fs';
import os from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
import crypto from 'node:crypto';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL('../..', import.meta.url)).replace(/[\\/]+$/, '');
const HERE = path.join(ROOT, 'tools', 'pack');
const args = process.argv.slice(2);
const opt = k => { const i = args.indexOf(k); return i >= 0 ? args[i + 1] : undefined; };
const OUT_NAME = 'project instructions.md';
const out = path.resolve(ROOT, opt('--out') ?? OUT_NAME);
// Claude Code keeps per-project memory under ~/.claude/projects/<project path with every non-alphanumeric as "-">/memory;
// a copy installed without one keeps it in docs/memory/ (see header.md step 4).
const DOCS_MEMORY = path.join(ROOT, 'docs', 'memory');
const memDir = opt('--memory') ?? (fs.existsSync(path.join(DOCS_MEMORY, 'MEMORY.md'))
  ? DOCS_MEMORY
  : path.join(os.homedir(), '.claude', 'projects', ROOT.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/g, '-'), 'memory'));

// What ships. Generated media, episodes and installs stay behind; the copy rebuilds what it needs.
const SKIP_DIRS = new Set(['node_modules', '.venv', '.git', '.bootstrap', '.claude', 'out', 'voice_auditions', '__pycache__']);
const FIXTURE_EPISODE = 'pipetest'; // the compositions' default slug; ships as JSON only (no audio)
const EXAMPLE_BRIEF = 'thumbnails/swap-pilot/brief.json'; // docs/pipeline/EPISODE.md points at it as the brief format
const KEEP_EMPTY = ['final/archive', 'final/thumbnails'];
function keep(rel) {
  if (rel === OUT_NAME) return false;
  if (rel.startsWith('docs/memory/') && path.resolve(memDir) === DOCS_MEMORY) return false; // ships as @memory/ instead
  if (rel.startsWith('final/')) return rel === 'final/README.md';
  if (rel.startsWith('public/episodes/')) return rel.startsWith(`public/episodes/${FIXTURE_EPISODE}/`) && /^[^/]+\.json$/.test(rel.split(`${FIXTURE_EPISODE}/`)[1]);
  if (rel.startsWith('public/audio/')) return !rel.endsWith('.wav'); // demo mixes come from their sfx scripts
  if (/^thumbnails\/[^/]+\//.test(rel) && !rel.startsWith('thumbnails/refs/')) return rel === EXAMPLE_BRIEF;
  return true;
}

// Changes that make the copy a fresh, key-less install. Idempotent, so a copy can repack itself.
const MEMORY_POINTER = /^Project memory \(the user's preferences and decisions\) lives in docs\/memory\/.*\r?\n(\r?\n)?/m;
const ELEVEN_NOTE = '> **ElevenLabs is not connected yet.** This copy was set up from `project instructions.md` without a working `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`. The first time one is added to `.env`, run `docs/ELEVENLABS_SETUP.md` before any voice work; its last step deletes this note. Until then, take episodes as far as the draft preview. (Fish Audio is separate and optional — only needed for `fish`-mode thumbnails; see `docs/FISH_SETUP.md`.)\n';
const eolOf = t => (t.includes('\r\n') ? '\r\n' : '\n');
const TRANSFORM = {
  'CLAUDE.md': t => {
    t = t.replace(MEMORY_POINTER, '');
    return t.includes('**ElevenLabs is not connected yet.**') ? t : t.replace(/^(# [^\r\n]*\r?\n)/, h => h + eolOf(t) + ELEVEN_NOTE.replace(/\n/g, eolOf(t)));
  },
  // the episode table lists finished videos, which don't ship: keep its header rows only
  'final/README.md': t => {
    const ls = t.split('\n'), at = ls.findIndex(l => l.startsWith('## Episodes'));
    let rows = 0;
    return ls.filter((l, i) => !(at >= 0 && i > at && l.startsWith('|') && ++rows > 2)).join('\n');
  },
};
const EXTRA = [
  ['docs/ELEVENLABS_SETUP.md', path.join(HERE, 'fresh', 'ELEVENLABS_SETUP.md')],
  ['@memory/project-elevenlabs-pending.md', path.join(HERE, 'fresh', 'project-elevenlabs-pending.md')],
  ['docs/FISH_SETUP.md', path.join(HERE, 'fresh', 'FISH_SETUP.md')],
  ['@memory/project-fish-pending.md', path.join(HERE, 'fresh', 'project-fish-pending.md')],
  // the /stickman command; .claude/ itself is skipped, so the local copy (which adds a demo shortcut) never ships
  ['.claude/commands/stickman.md', path.join(HERE, 'fresh', 'stickman.md')],
  // the review subagents, pinned to a smaller model (docs/pipeline/EPISODE.md steps 7.3 and 7.4)
  ['.claude/agents/revisor-episodio.md', path.join(ROOT, '.claude', 'agents', 'revisor-episodio.md')],
  ['.claude/agents/revisor-verificacao.md', path.join(ROOT, '.claude', 'agents', 'revisor-verificacao.md')],
];
const MEMORY_LINES = [
  '- [ElevenLabs pending](project-elevenlabs-pending.md) — no working ELEVENLABS_API_KEY at setup; run docs/ELEVENLABS_SETUP.md once one is added to .env\n',
  '- [Fish Audio pending](project-fish-pending.md) — Fish MCP NOT connected at setup; run docs/FISH_SETUP.md the first time Fish tools appear, only needed for fish-mode thumbnails\n',
];

const files = new Map(); // rel → Buffer
const dirs = [];
(function walk(dir) {
  const ents = fs.readdirSync(path.join(ROOT, dir), { withFileTypes: true });
  const relDir = dir.replace(/\\/g, '/');
  if (relDir && (ents.length === 0 || KEEP_EMPTY.includes(relDir))) dirs.push(relDir);
  for (const e of ents) {
    const rel = (dir ? `${dir}/` : '') + e.name;
    if (e.isDirectory()) { if (!SKIP_DIRS.has(e.name)) walk(rel); }
    else if (e.isFile() && keep(rel.replace(/\\/g, '/'))) files.set(rel.replace(/\\/g, '/'), fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, rel)));
  }
})('');
for (const [rel, fn] of Object.entries(TRANSFORM)) if (files.has(rel)) files.set(rel, Buffer.from(fn(files.get(rel).toString('utf8'))));
for (const [rel, src] of EXTRA) files.set(rel, fs.readFileSync(src));
if (fs.existsSync(memDir)) {
  for (const f of fs.readdirSync(memDir).filter(f => f.endsWith('.md'))) {
    let b = fs.readFileSync(path.join(memDir, f));
    if (f === 'MEMORY.md') {
      const t = b.toString('utf8'), e = eolOf(t);
      const add = MEMORY_LINES.filter(l => !t.includes(l.match(/\(([^)]+)\)/)[0])).map(l => l.replace(/\n/g, e));
      if (add.length) b = Buffer.from(t.replace(/(\r?\n)*$/, e) + add.join(''));
    }
    files.set(`@memory/${f}`, b);
  }
} else console.warn(`no memory folder at ${memDir}: packing without memory (pass --memory <dir>)`);

const BIN_EXT = /\.(png|jpe?g|webp|gif|ico|mp3|wav|flac|mp4|mov|webm|pyc|woff2?|ttf|otf|zip|gz)$/i;
const sha = b => crypto.createHash('sha256').update(b).digest('hex');
/** Text verbatim when it survives the round trip (strict UTF-8, uniform line endings, no marker-like lines), else base64. */
function encode(rel, buf) {
  const b64 = () => ({ enc: 'base64', body: buf.toString('base64').match(/.{1,76}/g) ?? [''], noeol: false });
  if (BIN_EXT.test(rel) || buf.includes(0)) return b64();
  let t = buf.toString('utf8');
  if (!Buffer.from(t, 'utf8').equals(buf)) return b64();
  let enc = 'text';
  if (t.includes('\r')) {
    const lf = t.replace(/\r\n/g, '\n');
    if (lf.includes('\r') || /(^|[^\r])\n/.test(t)) return b64(); // lone CR or mixed endings
    t = lf;
    enc = 'text-crlf';
  }
  const noeol = !t.endsWith('\n');
  const body = (noeol ? t : t.slice(0, -1)).split('\n');
  if (body.some(l => l.startsWith('@@@@ ') || l.startsWith('~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~'))) return b64();
  return { enc, body, noeol };
}

const order = [...files.keys()].sort((a, b) => (BIN_EXT.test(a) - BIN_EXT.test(b)) || (a < b ? -1 : 1));
const payload = ['~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ payload', '@@@@ PAYLOAD BEGIN', ...dirs.sort().map(d => `@@@@ DIR ${d}`)];
const groups = new Map();
for (const rel of order) {
  const buf = files.get(rel);
  const { enc, body, noeol } = encode(rel, buf);
  payload.push(`@@@@ FILE ${rel} | ${enc} | ${buf.length} | ${sha(buf)}${noeol ? ' | noeol' : ''}`, ...body, '@@@@ END');
  const g = rel.startsWith('@memory/') ? '@memory/' : rel.includes('/') ? rel.split('/')[0] + '/' : '(root)';
  const s = groups.get(g) ?? { n: 0, bytes: 0, bin: 0 };
  s.n++; s.bytes += buf.length; s.bin += enc === 'base64' ? 1 : 0;
  groups.set(g, s);
}
payload.push('@@@@ PAYLOAD END', '~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~', '');

const WHAT = {
  '(root)': '`CLAUDE.md` (the project rules), `HOW_TO_USE.md`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, Remotion and TypeScript config',
  'src/': 'the engine (rig, Stickman, actors, cameras, materials, effects), sets, cards, overlays, the episode pipeline and its self-tests',
  'tools/': 'build, episode, QA, review, stills, thumbnail and pack tools; Python sound design, music and idea tools',
  'docs/': 'style bible, story blueprint, idea engine, reviewer brief, ElevenLabs and Fish first-connect checklists, channel research with reference frames',
  'data/': 'idea-engine data: competitor titles, beat sheets, transcripts, patterns, ideas backlog',
  'public/': `the \`${FIXTURE_EPISODE}\` fixture episode (JSON only), empty \`music/\` and \`sfx/\``,
  'thumbnails/': 'config, the prompt template, the 3 reference images, an example brief',
  'final/': 'its README (finished videos land here)',
  '.claude/': 'the `/stickman <topic>` command and the `revisor-verificacao` subagent (sonnet)',
  '@memory/': "Claude's memory for this project (extracted into the new project's memory folder)",
};
const contents = ['| Path | Files | Size | What |', '|---|---|---|---|',
  ...[...groups].map(([g, s]) => `| \`${g}\` | ${s.n}${s.bin ? ` (${s.bin} binary)` : ''} | ${(s.bytes / 1024).toFixed(0)} KB | ${WHAT[g] ?? ''} |`)].join('\n');

// The hero as packed, so the outfit step stays right after a copy changes outfits and repacks itself.
const heroBody = /\bhero: \{([\s\S]*?)\},/.exec(files.get('src/cast.ts').toString('utf8'))?.[1];
if (!heroBody) throw new Error('no hero entry in src/cast.ts');
const heroEntry = `{ ${heroBody.replace(/\/\/[^\r\n]*/g, '').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim().replace(/,$/, '')} }`;
const heroField = k => new RegExp(`\\b${k}: '([^']+)'`).exec(heroBody)?.[1];
const heroGrep = [...new Set(['hoodie', heroField('top'), heroField('topColor'), heroField('accent')].filter(Boolean))].join('|');

const extractor = fs.readFileSync(path.join(HERE, 'extract.mjs'), 'utf8').replace(/\r\n/g, '\n').replace(/\n+$/, '');
let header = fs.readFileSync(path.join(HERE, 'header.md'), 'utf8').replace(/\r\n/g, '\n')

  .replace('{{CONTENTS}}', () => contents)
  .replace('{{HERO_ENTRY}}', () => heroEntry)
  .replace('{{HERO_GREP}}', () => heroGrep)
  .replace(/\{\{DATE\}\}/g, new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10))
  .replace(/\{\{FILE_COUNT\}\}/g, String(files.size));
header = header.replace(/\n*$/, '\n\n');
const headerEnd = header.split('\n').length - 1;
const body = payload.join('\n');
const mb = ((Buffer.byteLength(header) + Buffer.byteLength(body)) / 1e6).toFixed(1);
header = header.replace(/\{\{HEADER_END\}\}/g, String(headerEnd)).replace(/\{\{SIZE_MB\}\}/g, mb);
if (header.split('\n').includes('@@@@ PAYLOAD BEGIN')) throw new Error('header must not contain the payload marker line');
fs.writeFileSync(out, header + body);
console.log(`${path.relative(ROOT, out)}: ${files.size} files, ${dirs.length} empty folders, ${mb} MB, header ${headerEnd} lines`);

// Progress of a running build-episode.mjs: step, a bar, frames, elapsed time and the estimated time left.
//   node tools/progress.mjs <slug>            → one snapshot
//   node tools/progress.mjs <slug> --watch    → refreshes every 3 s until the build is done (Ctrl+C to stop)
// Reads out/<slug>/progress.json, which build-episode.mjs writes as it goes.
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL('..', import.meta.url));
const args = process.argv.slice(2);
const slug = args.find(a => !a.startsWith('--'));
if (!slug) {
  console.error('usage: node tools/progress.mjs <slug> [--watch]');
  process.exit(1);
}
const file = path.join(ROOT, 'out', slug, 'progress.json');
const STEPS = { audit: 'auditoria da cena', audio: 'trilha sonora (voz, música, efeitos)', render: 'renderizando quadros', encode: 'codificando o vídeo', mux: 'juntando vídeo e áudio', sheets: 'folhas de contato', done: 'pronto', failed: 'FALHOU' };
const mmss = ms => { const s = Math.max(0, Math.round(ms / 1000)); return `${Math.floor(s / 60)}:${String(s % 60).padStart(2, '0')}`; };

function snapshot() {
  if (!fs.existsSync(file)) return { text: `nenhuma build com progresso para "${slug}" (o arquivo ${path.relative(ROOT, file)} não existe)`, end: true };
  let p;
  try { p = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8')); } catch { return { text: '(lendo…)', end: false }; }
  const lines = [`${slug}${p.range ? ` [trecho ${p.range[0]}–${p.range[1]} s]` : ''} — ${STEPS[p.step] || p.step}`];
  if ((p.step === 'render' || p.step === 'encode') && p.total) {
    const k = p.done / p.total, n = 30, fill = Math.round(k * n);
    lines.push(`[${'█'.repeat(fill)}${'░'.repeat(n - fill)}] ${(100 * k).toFixed(1)}%  ${p.done}/${p.total} quadros${p.step === 'encode' ? ' codificados' : ''}`);
    if (p.eta) lines.push(`faltam ~${p.eta} (estimativa do Remotion)`);
  }
  lines.push(`tempo total da build: ${mmss((p.step === 'done' ? p.updated : Date.now()) - p.started)}`);
  const stale = Date.now() - p.updated > 120000 && !['done', 'failed'].includes(p.step);
  if (stale) lines.push(`(sem atualização há ${mmss(Date.now() - p.updated)} — a build pode ter parado)`);
  if (p.step === 'done' && p.final) lines.push(`arquivo: ${p.final}`);
  return { text: lines.join('\n'), end: ['done', 'failed'].includes(p.step) };
}

if (!args.includes('--watch')) {
  console.log(snapshot().text);
} else {
  const tick = () => {
    const s = snapshot();
    process.stdout.write('\x1b[2J\x1b[H' + s.text + '\n');
    if (s.end) process.exit(0);
  };
  tick();
  setInterval(tick, 3000);
}
